expected_release_bundle_sha256_note: computed by scripts/export_aeon_desktop_model.py on the reconciliation head on Linux. HONEST FINDING: torch.save produces a ZIP archive whose bytes include per-write timestamps (test_exporter_produces_tensor_deterministic_output_across_runs confirmed byte-hash divergence across two consecutive in-process saves). CROSS-MACHINE and CROSS-RUN byte-hash determinism is therefore NOT a property of the current exporter. The release manifest instead binds:  (i) the SHIPPED bundle's SHA-256 (stamped at export time)  (ii) the exact bytes of every packed tensor (verified via torch.equal after weights_only=True reload). Consumers verify their local model file against manifests/release_manifest.json.model_artifact_sha256, not against a hash pinned in this repository. For truly deterministic cross-machine bundles the exporter would need to write raw tensor bytes + a JSON manifest instead of relying on torch.save — deferred as a follow-up.
